newsitem.title: USA: U.S SPOT PRODS - GASOLINES SURGE ON REFINERY SNAG.
newsitem.headline: U.S SPOT PRODS - GASOLINES SURGE ON REFINERY SNAG.

text.p: U.S. gasoline prices rallied sharply Wednesday as both NYMEX futures prices and spot market differentials gained ground on nearby supply fears.
News that Exxon suffered a unit outage at its huge Baytown, Texas refinery sparked a buying frenzy in the Gulf, New York Harbor and the Midwest as traders sought to secure supplies.
On the NYMEX, September gasoline futures gained 2.37 cents to end the day at 66.08 cents a gallon and September heating oil futures firmed 0.94 cents to settle at 56.04 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF

Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline differentials shot higher by late day, with traders reporting a deal done as high as 0.85 cents under the September NYMEX, a gain of about 1.75 cents from late Tuesday.

Exxon admitted to taking its 110,000 barrel-per-day catalytic cracker out of service following a leak Tuesday, though the company would not estimate how long the unit would remain down. Market estimates ranged from about five days to as long as three weeks.
"That really got us going here today," one trader remarked.
Exxon refined product traders were seen buying gasoline earlier in the day while selling VGO, a feedstock for the cracker.
Reformulated A1 gasoline also jumped higher, with players quoting prompt deals as high as 6.00 cents over the M1 gasoline, or about 5.00 cents over the September NYMEX.

Premium grade 93-octane V1 conventional gasoline saw solid buying interest, with one player searching in vain for prompt barrels. Any-month V1 was quoted near 7.00 cents over the M1 grade, a gain of nearly 1.00 cent on the day.
NEW YORK HARBOR
NYH gasoline differentials also surged higher on tight prompt supplies, according to traders, led by the sharp rise in conventional gasoline levels.
Prompt conventional M2 gasoline differentials surged to 5.00 cents over the NYMEX by late day, up 1.30 cents from the previous day, according to market watchers.

Players continued to point to the downed catalytic cracking unit at Tosco's Bayway, New Jersey refinery as a key reason for the prompt gasoline tightness, though that unit is expected to return to service August 16-17.
Reformulated A2 jumped higher as a buyer paid 6.50 cents over the September futures, a gain of 0.50 cent on the day, market players said.
And prompt premium reformulated 93-octane D2 gasoline, which traders characterized as astronomically-priced, firmed to 17.50 cents over the September NYMEX on a trade reported near midday.

Tosco's restart of its crude oil unit at the Bayway refinery pressured prompt low sulphur diesel lower Tuesday, though those differentials rebounded about 0.10 cent to sit even with the September heating oil futures on the NYMEX, according to traders. However, a prompt parcel did trade at 0.20 cents under the screen early in the day.
MIDCONTINENT
Strength in the U.S. Gulf spread to the Midcontinent as concern grew that buying by Exxon in the Gulf translated to fewer barrels for Group Three and Chicago markets.
Group unleaded firmed a quarter cent to 5.50/6.00 cents a gallon, with deals done at 5.50 and 5.75 cents.
"There is a tightness for immediate barrels. Any barrels we would have expected from Gulf may not be coming," said a Midco trader, saying flush supplies earlier in the week have been wiped out.
Chicago market unleaded material held aloft at 4.50/4.75 cents in quiet activity. Any months were pegged 3.00/3.25 cents.
Distillate price movements remained more subdued than on the gasoline front. Chicago held at -1.25/1.00 cent under September futures and Group Three material 0.75/1.00 cent over the print.
Activity in general was light due to an industry golf outing in Austin, Texas.
- Matt Daily and Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk
